claims: As of March 2026, new COVID-19 variants are spreading in the U.S. and globally.
BA.3.2 is a highly mutated new COVID-19 variant.
BA.3.2 is nicknamed "Cicada".
Symptoms of new COVID-19 variants remain similar to previous Omicron subvariants.
Symptoms of new COVID-19 variants are generally reported as mild to moderate in vaccinated individuals.
Runny or stuffed nose is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026) and is often the first sign.
Sore throat is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026) and is described as severe, scratchy, or "razorblade throat" in some cases.
Headache is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026), often moderate and felt around the forehead or temples.
Dry cough is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026) and is mild but persistent.
Fatigue or extreme tiredness is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026).
Sneezing is a common symptom of current COVID-19 variants (2026) and is increasingly common in recent variants.
Body aches and muscle pain are common symptoms of current COVID-19 variants (2026).
Fever or chills are common symptoms of current COVID-19 variants (2026) and are less common than in earlier waves.
New COVID-19 variants frequently present with upper respiratory symptoms that are difficult to distinguish from a common cold or flu.
Loss of taste or smell has become less common compared to earlier in the pandemic.
Loss of taste or smell can still occur.
Newer subvariants tend to have symptoms appearing 2–4 days after exposure.
Symptoms previously appeared 5–7 days after exposure.
BA.3.2 can cause asymptomatic infections.
BA.3.2 remains sensitive to existing COVID antiviral drugs.
Rapid antigen tests are still effective at detecting these new variants.
